name: @w6w-apps/line
description: Send and receive messages through the LINE Messaging API: reply, push, multicast and broadcast, profiles, rich menus, and media.

w6w.longDescription:
LINE is the dominant chat platform in Japan (and widely used across Taiwan, Thailand and Indonesia), and the Messaging API is how a business account — a LINE Official Account — sends and receives chat messages, images, stickers and rich menus through it.

This app covers the core of that surface: replying to an inbound event with its one-time reply token, pushing or multicast/broadcasting a message outside that window, reading a bot's own identity and a user's profile, retrieving media a user sent, and managing rich menus (the tappable menu bar under a LINE Official Account's chat). Message content itself — text, image, sticker, template, flex — is accepted as LINE's own JSON message-object array rather than being re-modelled per type, since the vendor's schema already covers dozens of message shapes and re-deriving each as a separate typed action would multiply this app's surface without adding anything the vendor's own object model doesn't already say.

Authentication is a single long-lived channel access token, issued once from the LINE Developers Console and used as a Bearer token on every call — LINE's more elaborate JWT-assertion token-issuance flow is left to the console rather than reimplemented here.
